o1.biggest_strength: It aims at the Essentials 8+ churn leak, with the math traced to the data: $249k a month, $24k lost each month, and a revenue table with base and downside cases. Its test measures the real goal, churn of switchers against a random control group, and has clear go and stop numbers.
o1.biggest_mistake: Its base case assumes churn falls to 5% and half of customers switch, with no evidence behind either. It also lets the yearly-billing push sit as a side note instead of a quantified quick win.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put a numbers-backed yearly-billing nudge into the plan and the math, and justify the switch and churn assumptions from the Team 8+ and 4-to-7 bands.

o2.biggest_strength: A concrete pre-test data check (Team 8+ accounts with one active user), a ready pricing-page table, and sharp risks such as approvals possibly needing product work and big accounts paying less.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its main test only watches new logged-out visitors over 60 days. That cannot show the churn reduction the plan depends on, and it takes until February to launch. It also brushes off the yearly-billing quick win as missing the board window.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Test the plan on at-risk existing 8+ customers with a control group so churn is measured directly, and fold the yearly-billing nudge into the plan as the fast win.

reason: Both pick the same flat Agency plan and both do the math well. Output 1's test measures what matters, churn of switchers against a control group, and it includes the yearly-billing offer. Output 2's new-visitor test cannot show the churn benefit and dismisses the yearly quick win.
